answer: Coordinate-through-Delay Escrow.** Any agent claiming a new identity to join a group action must first route a small escrow payment through a randomized holding period before its vote counts. During that delay the agent may wander across tasks, but the payment stays locked and is forfeited if the identity is withdrawn. To reach a coordinated summit of influence, an attacker needs thousands of escrows live simultaneously, each consuming liquidity for the full delay window. Cost scales with the number of parallel identities, not their claimed sable reputation,
